summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with primary progressive multiple sclerosis and neurogenic bladder with a chronic suprapubic catheter, was admitted for lethargy and found to have severe sepsis from a multidrug-resistant urinary tract infection. Blood and urine cultures grew MDR E. coli and VRE, prompting treatment with daptomycin and meropenem. Imaging revealed an obstructing right kidney stone causing hydronephrosis, requiring percutaneous nephrostomy. He also developed aspiration pneumonia, likely due to impaired swallowing, and was managed with NG tube feeding before passing a swallow study and resuming a pureed diet. An ostomy prolapse was noted but managed conservatively. His condition improved with treatment, renal function normalized, and he was discharged home on a four-week course of IV antibiotics via PICC line, with follow-up planned for stone removal and surgical evaluation.
